discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of time-reversal-invariant (Z2) topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect
subfield: Condensed matter physics (topological phases of matter)
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can produce a new phase of matter, the quantum spin Hall insulator. This phase is protected by time-reversal symmetry and classified by a Z2 topological invariant, and it has helical edge states that conduct without backscattering. Their invariant, later extended to three dimensions, created the field of topological insulators and gave a model for the symmetry-protected topological classification that is now central to condensed matter physics. In 2007 Molenkamp's group gave decisive experimental proof in HgTe quantum wells. They measured quantised edge conductance that appears only above a critical well thickness, and later confirmed nonlocal helical transport. This combination of clean theory, a concrete material and unambiguous detection is rare. The discovery underlies today's topological superconductivity, Majorana platforms and the prospects for topologically protected quantum information.
